fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Front Driveway; Water Feature; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Walkway; Dense Vegetation; Open Lawn Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Water Feature; Dense Vegetation; Multiple Structures; Limited Side Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so arriving units do not mistake neighboring access points.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles along its full length to allow multiple units to stage or pass simultaneously.
• Identify a flat, open area near the detached structure where a second responding unit can park without blocking the drive.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so it does not narrow the usable driving surface or obstruct driver sightlines.
• Cut back dense vegetation that limits walking access along the sides of the main residence so responders can move between the front and rear on foot.
• Mark any walking path that connects the main residence to the detached structure so responders can locate it quickly under low-light or smoke conditions.
• Post the water feature location visibly near the driveway entrance so night operations crews are aware of its position before approaching on foot.
• Keep a clear walking path around the water feature so responders moving through the property at night or in reduced visibility do not approach it unexpectedly.
• Confirm that any gate or barrier controlling the single access point can be opened quickly from the outside without a key or code, or provide responders with access information in advance.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Water Feature; Scattered Shrubs; Grass Cover; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Along Driveway; Open Green Space; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Trees; Woody Debris
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris piles from areas near the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create open space between individual trees and the building.
• Trim low-hanging branches on scattered trees near the house to reduce the path fire can travel from the ground up into the tree canopy.
• Cut back shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the house.
• Mow or cut the grass cover around the house, especially during dry periods, to reduce the amount of ground-level material that can carry fire.
• Remove or thin the mixed vegetation growing close to the structure on all accessible sides.
• Trim back vegetation growing along the driveway so branches do not hang over the road surface and vehicles can pass freely.
• Keep the driveway edges clear of shrubs and tall grass that could block movement or visibility along the drive.
• Clear a walking path around the rear of the structure by removing shrubs, woody debris, and low branches that limit access.
• Separate shrubs and small trees near the house so there are visible gaps between individual plants and between plants and the structure.
• Remove dead branches, fallen limbs, and leaf litter from beneath trees near the house.
• Keep the grass and low vegetation nearest the water feature trimmed short so it does not act as a continuous path toward the structure.
